nodes.name: Triple (mu1, tau1, delta_q)
nodes.statement: \emph{Triple ($\hat{\mu}_1, \tau_{1}, \delta_q$)}: Because $$\hat{\mu}_1(p) =1 \text{ and } \hat{\mu}_1(q)=0$$ the transition $t$ can be enabled without firing $t_{in}$ by a reachable marking \mbox{of $(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_1)$} due to \mbox{Proposition \ref{prop_cpnetsubnetsperpetual}}, part 4). Because $\hat{N}$ is a $T$-net Proposition \ref{prop_perpetualtsystem}, part 1) provides a pair $$(\tau_q,\delta_q) \in en_{sd}(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_1)_q \text{ with } \Vert \hat{\mu}_1 \Vert_{\delta_q}=0$$ see Figure \ref{fig_lucent}, left-hand side.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition on CP-nets part 4 and T-system part 1 give a token-free path to q.
nodes.section: 6 Enabling equivalence and marking equality in $CP$-subnets of \\ perpetual free-choice systems

nodes.name: Pair (mu2, tau)
nodes.statement: \emph{Pair ($\hat{\mu}_2,\tau_p)$}: By enabling equivalence $$\tau_q \in en(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_1) \implies \tau_q \in en(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_2)$$
nodes.statement_short: Enabling equivalence transfers tau_q.
nodes.section: 6 Enabling equivalence and marking equality in $CP$-subnets of \\ perpetual free-choice systems

nodes.name: Triple (mu2, tau_p, delta_p)
nodes.statement: \emph{Triple ($\hat{\mu}_2,\tau_p,\delta_p$)}: The transition $\tau_q \in en(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_2)$ has a pre-place marked \mbox{at $\hat{\mu}_2$}. \noindent Proposition \ref{prop_cpnetsubnetsperpetual}, part 4), applied to the path $\delta_q$, shows that $t$ is enabled at a reachable marking of $(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_2)$. Because $\hat{\mu}_2(p)=0$ Proposition \ref{prop_perpetualtsystem}, part 1) provides a pair $$(\tau_p,\delta_p) \in en_{sd}(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_2)_p \text{ with } \Vert \hat{\mu}_2 \Vert_{\delta_p}=0,$$ see Figure \ref{fig_lucent}, middle.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain a token-free path to p at mu_2.
nodes.section: 6 Enabling equivalence and marking equality in $CP$-subnets of \\ perpetual free-choice systems

nodes.name: Triple (mu1, tau_p, delta_p)
nodes.statement: \emph{Triple ($\hat{\mu}_1,\tau_p,\delta_p$)}: By enabling equivalence $$\tau_p \in en(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_2) \implies \tau_p \in en(\hat{N},\hat{\mu}_1)$$ Figure \ref{fig_lucent}, right-hand side shows $\hat{\mu}_1$. After firing $\hat{\mu}_1 \xrightarrow{\tau_p} \mu^\prime$ the segment $$\delta^\prime :=(\tau_p,...,p) \text{ of } \delta_p \subset \hat{N}$$ has token count $$\Vert \mu^\prime \Vert_{\delta^\prime}\geq 2,$$ but due to Proposition \ref{prop_cpnetsubnetsperpetual}, part 2) $$\Vert \mu^\prime \Vert_{\delta^\prime}\leq 1.$$ The contradiction refutes the assumption of the indirect proof, hence $$\hat{\mu}_1=\hat{\mu}_2$$
nodes.statement_short: Two tokens on a CP-subnet path contradict the one-token bound.
nodes.section: 6 Enabling equivalence and marking equality in $CP$-subnets of \\ perpetual free-choice systems

nodes.name: Part 2: common shutdown sequence
nodes.statement: Due to part 1) $$\mu_1|\hat{N}=\mu_2|\hat{N}.$$ Remark \ref{rem_existencestructuredynamics} implies: Each marking $\mu_j,\ j=1,2,$ enables a shutdown sequence \mbox{of $\hat{N}$}. Because a shutdown sequence has only transitions from $\hat{N}_T \setminus \{t_{in}\}$, each shutdown sequence enabled at $\mu_1$ is also a shutdown sequence enabled at $\mu_2$, and vice \mbox{ versa.}
nodes.statement_short: Equal restrictions and shutdown sequences inside the CP-subnet give a common one.
nodes.section: 6 Enabling equivalence and marking equality in $CP$-subnets of \\ perpetual free-choice systems

nodes.name: Complement live and safe
nodes.statement: Remark \ref{rem_existencestructuredynamics}, part 3) implies that $(\overline{N},\overline{\mu})$ is a live and safe free-choice system.
nodes.statement_short: Remark on CP-subnets gives a live safe complement.

nodes.statement:
The clusters $$cl \subset N 	ext{ and } \overline{cl} \subset \overline{N}$$ have the same places. Hence $$
u_{post} \geq \mu_{cl} \implies 
u_{post}=\mu_{cl}$$ As a consequence $$\overline{
u}_{post}=\mu_{cl}|\overline{N}=\mu_{\overline{cl}}$$ is a regeneration marking of $(\overline{N},\overline{\mu})$.
nodes.statement_short: Same places give equality with mu_cl.

nodes.name: Compare enabledness
nodes.statement: The idea of the proof is to compare the enabledness of each transition $t \in \overline{N}$ before and after firing $\sigma$. The proof shows: A transition $t$ is enabled \textit{before} firing $\sigma$ at both \mbox{markings $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$} or at none of them if and only \textit{after} firing $\sigma$ the transition is enabled at both markings $(\mu_{1,sd},\mu_{2,sd})$ or at none of them.
nodes.statement_short: Enabledness agreement is preserved by firing sigma.

nodes.name: Ingredients
nodes.statement: Besides \mbox{Proposition \ref{prop_perpetualtsystem}} and \ref{prop_markingequality} the main ingredient is the fact that a live and \mbox{bounded $T$-system} is cyclic.
nodes.statement_short: Uses the T-system and CP-subnet propositions plus cyclicity of live bounded T-systems.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Restrictions to the T-net
nodes.statement: We set $$\overline{\mu}_j:=\mu_j|\overline{N},\ j=1,2.$$ Because $\overline{N} \subset N$ is place-bordered: For each transition $t \in \overline{N}$ and for $j=1,2$ holds $$t \in en(N,\mu_j) \iff t \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_j)$$
nodes.statement_short: Restrict markings to the final T-net; enabledness agrees.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Part 1: global shutdown sequence
nodes.statement: For each $i \in I$ Proposition \ref{prop_markingequality} provides a common shutdown \mbox{sequence $\sigma_i$} of $\hat{N}_i$ with respect to the markings $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$. For each pair $i \neq k \in I$ the pre-sets of the non way-in transitions of $\hat{N}_i$ and $\hat{N}_k$ are disjoint, which proves part 1).
nodes.statement_short: Common shutdown sequences per CP-subnet with disjoint pre-sets concatenate.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Part 2: marking difference
nodes.statement: If $p\in \overline{N} \subset N$ is not a way-in place of $\overline{N}$ then for $j=1,2$ $$\mu_k(p)=\mu_{k,sd}(p).$$ And for a way-in place $p\in \overline{N}_{P,in}$ the change $\mu_{k,sd}(p)-\mu_k(p)$ of both markings depends only on the transitions of $\sigma$. Hence the change is the same whether \mbox{firing $\sigma$} at $\mu_1$ or at $\mu_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Only way-in places change, by the same amount.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Part 3: reachability and enabling equivalence
nodes.statement_short: Reachability via cyclicity, then enabling equivalence of the shut-down markings.

nodes.name: Perpetuality and reachability
nodes.statement: For $j=1,2$ Proposition \ref{prop_propagatingperpetuality} implies that $(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{j,sd})$ is perpetual with regeneration marking $\mu_{\overline{cl}}$. Live $T$-systems are cyclic, hence $\overline{\mu}_{j,sd}$ is reachable in $(\overline{N},\mu_{\overline{cl}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Propagating perpetuality and cyclicity give reachability.

nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Non-critical transitions
nodes.statement: i) \emph{Non-critical transitions}: If $t \in \overline{N}_T\setminus \overline{N}_{T,crit}$ then $$^\bullet t \cap \overline{N}_{P,in}=\emptyset.$$ Hence firing $\sigma$ does not change the marking on $^\bullet t$. As a consequence \end{flushleft} $$\left [en(N,\mu_1)=en(N,\mu_2)\right] \implies \left[t \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}) \iff t \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd})\right]$$
nodes.statement_short: Their pre-sets are untouched by sigma.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Critical transitions
nodes.statement_short: Indirect argument producing an alternating chain of critical transitions.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Indirect assumption
nodes.statement: The proof of the claim is indirect. Assume the existence of a critical transition $t \in \overline{N}_{T,crit}$ which violates enabling equivalence, w.l.o.g. $$t\in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}) \setminus en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd})$$ Then $t$ is enabled at neither marking $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$, and firing $\sigma$ at $\mu_1$ enables $t$, but firing $\sigma$ at $\mu_2$ does not. \mbox{Hence $t$} has at least two pre-places, w.l.o.g. $t$ has exactly two pre-places $$^\bullet t=\{p,q\} \text{ with } p \in \overline{N}_{P,in}$$ satisfying $$(\mu_1(p),\mu_1(q))=(0,1) \text{ and } (\mu_2(p),\mu_2(q))=(0,0)$$ $$(\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}(p),\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}(q))=(1,1) \text{ and } (\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}(p),\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}(q))=(1,0).$$
nodes.statement_short: A critical transition enabled at one shut-down marking only; fix its pre-place markings.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Path to q
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop_perpetualtsystem}, part 2 i), applied to the perpetual $T$-system $(\overline{N},\mu_{\overline{cl}})$ and its reachable \mbox{marking $\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}$}, provides a pair $$(\tau,\delta) \in en(\overline{N}, \overline{\mu}_{2,sd})_q,\ \tau \neq t, \text{ with } \Vert \overline{\mu}_{2,sd} \Vert_\delta =0 \text{ and } t_{\overline{cl}} \notin \delta^\prime$$ for the segment $$\delta^\prime:=(\tau,...,q) \text{ of }\delta.$$ In particular $\tau \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd})$.
nodes.statement_short: Part 2 i) gives a token-free path to q avoiding t_cl.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: tau not enabled at mu1
nodes.statement: The transition $\tau$ satisfies $$\tau \notin en(\overline{N}, \overline{\mu}_{1,sd}):$$ Otherwise, after firing $\overline{\mu}_{1,sd} \xrightarrow{\tau} \mu^\prime$ the path $\delta^\prime$ has token count $$\Vert \mu^\prime \Vert_{\delta^\prime}\geq 2$$ because $\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}(q)=1$. Then Proposition \ref{prop_perpetualtsystem}, part 2 ii) implies the contradiction $$\Vert \mu^\prime \Vert_{\delta^\prime}\leq 1$$
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise firing tau gives two tokens on a path, contradicting part 2 ii).
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: tau is critical
nodes.statement:
By the previous step and by the assumed enabling equivalence $$	au 
otin en(\overline{N}, \overline{\mu}_{1,sd})\implies 	au 
otin en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_1) \implies 	au 
otin en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_2)$$ As a consequence $$	au \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}) \setminus en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_2),$$ and the transition $	au$ becomes enabled at a reachable marking of $(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_2)$ not until firing a way-out transition $t_{out} \in \hat{N}$. Hence $	au \in \overline{N}_{T,crit}$ is a further critical transition with $$	au \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}) \setminus en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}).$$
nodes.statement_short: tau is a further critical transition with the roles reversed.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: t differs from t_cl
nodes.statement: The previous result implies that at least one pre-place $\tau$ is marked at $\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}$ due to the firing of $t_{out}$. As a consequence $$t_{\overline{cl}} \neq t:$$ Otherwise the enabling $t \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd})$, the greediness of $\overline{cl}$, and the fact, that places of \mbox{a $T$-net} do not branch, imply $t=\tau$, which has been excluded above.
nodes.statement_short: Greediness excludes t = t_cl.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: We now iterate the whole argument above: It derives from the critical transition $$t_1:=t \in \overline{N}_{T,crit} \cap \left(en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}) \setminus en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd})\right)$$ a second critical transition $$t_2:=\tau \in \overline{N}_{T,crit} \cap \left(en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}) \setminus en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd})\right)$$ and a path $$\delta_1:=\delta=(t_2,...,q_1,t_1) \subset \overline{N} \text{ with } \Vert \overline{\mu}_{1,sd} \Vert_{\delta_1}=1,\ \Vert \overline{\mu}_{2,sd} \Vert_{\delta_1}=0 \text{ and } t_{\overline{cl}} \notin \delta_1$$ see Figure \ref{fig_enablingcriticaltransitions}.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat to get a second critical transition and a connecting path.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Marked circuit avoiding t_cl
nodes.statement: After finitely many steps we obtain a family of critical transitions $$t_k \in \overline{N}_{T,crit}, \ k=1,...,m,$$ and elementary paths $$\delta_k=(t_{k+1},...,q_k,t_k) \subset \overline{N},\ k=1,...,m-1,\ t_{cl} \notin \delta_k,$$ satisfying $$\Vert \overline{\mu}_{1,sd} \Vert_{\delta_k}=\begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } k \text{ odd} \\ 0 & \text{if } k \text{ even} \end{cases},\ \Vert \overline{\mu}_{2,sd} \Vert_{\delta_k}=\begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } k \text{ even} \\ 0 & \text{if } k \text{ odd} \end{cases}$$ Because $\overline{N}$ has only finitely many critical transitions, a subset of these paths concatenates and induces a circuit $$\gamma \subset \overline{N} \text{ with } t_{\overline{cl}} \notin \gamma.$$ The circuit $\gamma$ satisfies $$\Vert \mu_{\overline{cl}} \Vert_\gamma= \Vert \overline{\mu}_{1,sd} \Vert_\gamma= \Vert \overline{\mu}_{2,sd} \Vert_\gamma \geq 1$$ Hence $\gamma$ has at least one elementary subcircuit which is marked at $\mu_{\overline{cl}}$. The result contradicts the fundamental property of perpetual $T$-systems because the subcircuit does not contain $t_{\overline{cl}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Finitely many critical transitions close a marked circuit avoiding t_cl, a contradiction.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: All critical transitions agree
nodes.statement: The contradiction refutes the assumption that the critical transition $t=t_1$ violates enabling equivalence. Hence all critical transitions $t \in \overline{N}_{T,crit}$ satisfy \end{flushleft} $$t \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}) \iff t \in en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd})$$
nodes.statement_short: Hence critical transitions respect enabling equivalence.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Enabling equivalence
nodes.statement: iii) \emph{Enabling equivalence}: The two previous parts show $$en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}) = en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}),$$ which finishes the proof of the Proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Combine both cases.
nodes.section: 7 Propagating perpetuality and enabling equivalence along \\ $CP$-exhaustions

nodes.name: Fix the perpetual system
nodes.statement: Consider a perpetual free-choice system $(N,\mu_0)$ with a regeneration \mbox{cluster $cl \subset N$} and its regeneration marking $\mu_{cl}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the system, regeneration cluster and marking.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: CP-exhaustion
nodes.statement: \emph{$CP$-exhaustion}: Theorem \ref{theor_existencecpexhaustion} provides a $cl$-adapted $CP$-exhaustion of $N$ $${(\hat{N}_i)}_{i \in I},\ I=\{0,...,n\} \subset \mathbb{N},$$ with $CP$-subnets $\hat{N}_i \subset N$, complements $$\overline{N}_i:=\overline{N}_{i-1}\setminus \hat{N}_i,\ \overline{N}_{-1}:=N,$$ and the final strongly connected $T$-net $$\overline{N}:=N\setminus \dot\bigcup_{i\in N} \hat{N_i}$$ The disjoint union of full subnets of $N$ $$N_{exh}:= \overline{N}\ \dot\cup\ \hat{N}_0\ \dot\cup \ ...\ \dot\cup \ \hat{N}_n$$ is a subnet of $N$ with the same nodes as $N$. The regeneration \mbox{cluster $cl$} intersects each complement $\overline{N}_i,\ i \in I,$ and $\overline{N}$ in a non-empty cluster. Set $$\overline{cl}:= \overline{N} \cap cl \subset \overline{N}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the existence theorem for a cl-adapted CP-exhaustion.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: Enabling-equivalent pair
nodes.statement: To continue the proof assume a pair of reachable markings $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ of $(N,\mu_0)$ with \end{flushleft} $$en(N,\mu_1)=en(N,\mu_2).$$
nodes.statement_short: Take two enabling-equivalent reachable markings.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: Equality on CP-subnets
nodes.statement: \emph{Marking equality in the $CP$-subnets}: Proposition \ref{prop_markingequality} implies for \mbox{each $i \in I$} $$(\mu_1-\mu_2)|\hat{N}_i=0$$
nodes.statement_short: Proposition on adapted CP-subnets gives equality there.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: Equality on the final T-net
nodes.statement: \emph{Marking equality in the final $T$-net}: Proposition \ref{prop_propagatingenablingequivalence} considers simultaneously the collection of all $CP$-subnets $\hat{N}_i,\ i \in I$. The proposition provides a global shutdown sequence $\sigma$ enabled at both markings $\mu_j,\ j=1,2,$ $$\mu_j \xrightarrow{\sigma} \mu_{j,sd}$$ such that the resulting markings of $\overline{N}$ $$\overline{\mu}_{j,sd}:=\mu_{j,sd}|\overline{N}$$ \begin{itemize} \item are reachable in the $T$-system $(\overline{N},\mu_{\overline{cl}})$, \item satisfy $$\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}-\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}=(\mu_1-\mu_2)|\overline{N}$$ \item and are enabling equivalent $$en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd})=en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}).$$ \end{itemize} \noindent Proposition \ref{prop_propagatingperpetuality} implies that $(\overline{N},\mu_{\overline{cl})})$ is perpetual. Proposition \ref{prop_tsystemlucent} concludes $$\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}-\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}=0.$$ As a consequence $$(\mu_{1} - \mu_{2})|\overline{N}=0$$ Combining part 2) and 3) of the proof shows $$\mu_1=\mu_2$$ and finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Global shutdown plus lucency of perpetual T-systems give equality on the T-net, hence overall.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: Global shutdown sequence
nodes.statement: \emph{Marking equality in the final $T$-net}: Proposition \ref{prop_propagatingenablingequivalence} considers simultaneously the collection of all $CP$-subnets $\hat{N}_i,\ i \in I$. The proposition provides a global shutdown sequence $\sigma$ enabled at both markings $\mu_j,\ j=1,2,$ $$\mu_j \xrightarrow{\sigma} \mu_{j,sd}$$ such that the resulting markings of $\overline{N}$ $$\overline{\mu}_{j,sd}:=\mu_{j,sd}|\overline{N}$$ \begin{itemize} \item are reachable in the $T$-system $(\overline{N},\mu_{\overline{cl}})$, \item satisfy $$\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}-\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}=(\mu_1-\mu_2)|\overline{N}$$ \item and are enabling equivalent $$en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{1,sd})=en(\overline{N},\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}).$$
nodes.statement_short: Propagating enabling equivalence to the final T-net.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: Lucency of the T-system
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop_propagatingperpetuality} implies that $(\overline{N},\mu_{\overline{cl})})$ is perpetual. Proposition \ref{prop_tsystemlucent} concludes $$\overline{\mu}_{1,sd}-\overline{\mu}_{2,sd}=0.$$ As a consequence $$(\mu_{1} - \mu_{2})|\overline{N}=0$$
nodes.statement_short: Perpetuality and Proposition (T-systems lucent) give equality on the T-net.
nodes.section: 8 Statement and proof of van der Aalst's theorem

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining part 2) and 3) of the proof shows $$\mu_1=\mu_2$$ and finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Combine parts 2 and 3: mu_1 = mu_2.
